(i) We take curry with rice. The curry does not taste good if we do not use $\text{NaCl}$ in it.

(ii) $\text{NaCl}$ is used in industries to prepare $\text{NaOH}$ compound.

(iii) $\text{NaCl}$ is used in drug industries to manufacture salines for diarrhoea or dehydration.

Chemical name of baking soda or table soda is sodium hydrogen carbonate ($\text{NaHCO}_3$). Baking soda is also called sodium bicarbonate. Baking powder is produced when tartaric acid ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_6\text{O}_6$) is mixed with baking soda ($\text{NaHCO}_3$).

Baking powder is usually used in making cakes.

Baking Soda can be prepared from ammonia gas, salt, water and carbon-di-oxide. At first, saturated solution of $\text{NaCl}$ is prepared by dissolving $\text{NaCl}$ in water. Again this solution is saturated by blowing $\text{NH}_3$ gas into the saturated solution. Then carbon-di-oxide gas is blown into the $\text{NaCl}$ solution saturated by $\text{NH}_3$. At this stage, at first $\text{CO}_2$, $\text{NH}_3$, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ together produce Ammonium Hydrogen Carbonate ($\text{NH}_4\text{HCO}_3$). Then the ammonium hydrogen carbonate reacts with sodium chloride and produces sodium hydrogen carbonate or baking soda.

$$\text{CO}_2 + \text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow \text{NH}_4\text{HCO}_3$$

$$\text{NH}_4\text{HCO}_3 + \text{NaCl} \longrightarrow \text{NaHCO}_3 + \text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$$

Baking soda is separated from the reaction pot and then tartaric acid is mixed with it. This mixture is called baking powder.

During making cakes, baking powder is mixed with the flour of cake and heated. Baking soda reacts with tartaric acid ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_6\text{O}_6$) in the mixture and produces sodium tartaret ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_4\text{Na}_2\text{O}_6$), $\text{CO}_2$ gas and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Cakes rise up because of this $\text{CO}_2$ gas.

$$2\text{NaHCO}_3 + \text{C}_4\text{H}_6\text{O}_6 \longrightarrow \text{C}_4\text{H}_4\text{Na}_2\text{O}_6 + 2\text{CO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
